stem.text: A particle moves in the plane with velocity vector \( v(t) = \left\langle 5 t, \cos{\left(\frac{t}{2} \right)} \right\rangle \), with t in seconds and distance in meters, and it is at the origin at \( t = 0 \). Using a calculator, find the total distance the particle travels over \( 0 \le t \le 3 \). Show the setup for the calculation, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: From the velocity, the components are \( \frac{dx}{dt} = 5 t \) and \( \frac{dy}{dt} = \cos{\left(\frac{t}{2} \right)} \).
The length is \( \int_{0}^{3} \sqrt{\left(5 t\right)^{2} + \left(\cos{\left(\frac{t}{2} \right)}\right)^{2}}\,dt \), the integral of the speed.
worked_solution.rule_named: arc length of a parametric curve

options.derivation: the straight-line distance from the start to the end, the magnitude of the displacement
(dx/dt)^2 written as 5 t^2, the coefficient left unsquared
the two rates added, the integral of dx/dt + dy/dt
